_notes: Italian contrast pairs. Lookup: pattern → counterpart pattern. When user answers a question whose pattern is a key here, 70% probability the next question is drawn from the bank where pattern === counterpart, IF such a question exists and hasn't been seen this session. Italian-specific priorities: (1) auxiliary selection (essere vs avere — verbs of movement / pronominal take essere, transitives take avere). (2) passato prossimo vs imperfetto — the punctual vs descriptive/habitual axis. (3) ci vs ne pronouns — locative ci against partitive ne. (4) congiuntivo vs indicativo — including the imperfect congiuntivo for hypothesis. (5) tu vs Lei — informal vs formal second person, both directions. (6) articolo determinativo vs partitivo — 'lo zucchero' vs 'dello zucchero'. (7) prep articolata a vs in — 'al/alla' vs 'nel/nella' on city/region/country split. (8) imperativo tu vs imperativo Lei — informal vs formal command. Disabled in bosses and review mode.
_asymmetric_notes: Some entries are one-way intentionally (e.g. aux-essere-pronominal → aux-avere-transitive, imperfetto-abitudine → passato-prossimo-vs-imperfetto): the reverse case is already covered by another key and we don't want to over-pair the dominant pattern.
